name: PostgreSQL

inputs.name: ca
inputs.label: CA certificate file (PEM) - needed with TLS verify, a public CA too: its root (e.g. ISRG Root X1)

access: CONNECT on the database, USAGE on the schema and SELECT on its tables

schema_check.statement: SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_catalog.pg_namespace WHERE nspname = {v}) THEN (CASE WHEN has_schema_privilege({v}, 'USAGE') THEN 'ok' ELSE 'denied' END) ELSE COALESCE((SELECT 'case:' || MIN(nspname) FROM pg_catalog.pg_namespace WHERE lower(nspname) = lower({v})), 'missing') END
schema_check.case: PostgreSQL folds an unquoted name to lower case

tips: Names arrive in upper case (FILM, TITLE): query them without quotes.
NUMERIC columns arrive as VARCHAR, so cast them to compute: CAST(RENTAL_RATE AS DECIMAL(10,2)).

A column of a domain type (pagila's FILM.RELEASE_YEAR) or an extension type such as vector cannot be read, and BYTEA reads as the text 'bytea NOT SUPPORTED': leave such columns out of the SELECT list.
notes: The adapter JAR already contains pgJDBC 42.7.14; the driver pin is the same version so the two copies never disagree.

verify checks the server certificate AND its host name against the CA given with --set ca=<PEM file or bundle>, a public CA's root too (the loader's own CA store is empty on Exasol Personal 2.4): the one certificate that signs the server travels in the URL (SingleCertValidatingFactory), because the loader's Java sandbox denies file reads. require only encrypts, with NonValidatingFactory named: the default LibPQFactory reads ~/.postgresql/ for a client key, which the loader's Java sandbox refuses, and pgjdbc reports that as "Your security policy has prevented the connection from being attempted" (measured on Exasol Personal 2.4).
